root_idea.summary: An orientation of turning aside, deviation, and lack of fixed stability.
root_idea.development: The root develops from physical or directional turning and unstable movement into secret or crafty approach, evasion, pursuit, reciprocal maneuvering, and related senses of turning something through a medium or against an opponent.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The canonical Form I Quranic verb is displayed under its normalized perfect-tense dictionary citation form.

senses.definition: To turn aside secretly toward someone or something; to go or return to it by a discreet or crafty movement.
senses.usage_conditions: Used with إِلَى. In the Quran it describes turning toward the idols and going secretly to one's family; the movement is presented as purposeful and involving a form of maneuvering or guile.

senses.definition: To turn against or advance upon someone or something by stratagem, with the aim of overpowering or striking it.
senses.usage_conditions: Used with عَلَى. In the Quranic construction فَرَاغَ عَلَيْهِمْ ضَرْبًا بِالْيَمِينِ, the sense is a covert or artful advance against the object, leading to an act of striking.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To turn aside or away, move this way and that, deviate, or elude and dodge; to swerve from a person, path, truth, or intended course.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A general Classical Arabic use, including movement of a fox, person, game, or road. The Quranic إِلَى and عَلَى constructions are treated separately above.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To seek quickly an object of need from someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form I use describing the pursuit of an urgently desired object or favor.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To smear, season, imbue, or soak bread or a morsel with grease, gravy, dripping, or clarified butter.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A tropical Form II use applied to food that is turned through or saturated with fat.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To practise deceit or artifice with someone; to try to deceive, circumvent, or induce that person to turn.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form III reciprocal or transitive construction, including maneuvering toward or away from a person or matter by blandishment or guile.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Wrestling or struggling together, with each opponent maneuvering against the other.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional Form III verbal-noun use for reciprocal physical grappling.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To seek, pursue, search for, or desire a thing, especially one difficult to obtain; to pursue game or a runaway object.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The Form IV verb may also describe devising or plotting in pursuit of an objective; the explicitly cross-referenced Form VIII form has the same sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To roll or turn oneself over; to become befouled or bedaubed in mud.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form V intransitive use describing bodily movement or the resulting state of being muddied.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Abundance, plenty, or a state of having plentiful herbage, wealth, or the goods and comforts of life.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes the idiomatic expression خيرٌ رَوَاغٌ, abundant good or wealth, and the state expressed by في الرِّيَاغِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The wrestling place of a people.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The two forms are given as variant forms of the noun for the place where wrestling takes place.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An evasion, elusion, shift, wile, artifice, plot, or stratagem.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A diminutive lexical form derived from the notion of turning aside by a device or trick.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One habitually given to turning aside, moving evasively, or eluding and dodging; an appellation for a fox.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The comparative أَرْوَغُ expresses a greater or greatest degree of this evasive tendency.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Deviating; specifically, a road that turns away from the main road or a side road.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used adjectivally with طريق and substantivized for a road diverging from the main route.

cautions: The two Quranic senses are distinguished chiefly by construction: إِلَى marks a secret turn toward or return, while عَلَى marks a turn against or advance upon.

Printed citation traditions for the turning-against passage are not uniform; the modern location 37:93 is used here from the independently supplied Quran identification rather than by converting a historical bracketed citation.
